Clothing & appearance 1

Shop for clothes and talk about what to wear in Thai. This first part covers the wardrobe basics and the fitting room: เสื้อยืด (t-shirt), กางเกงยีนส์ (jeans), กระโปรง (skirt) and รองเท้า (shoes), plus asking to ลอง (try on), finding the ห้องลอง (fitting room), and sorting out ไซส์ (size) when something's คับ (too tight) or พอดี (just right). It also covers dressing for the weather and the Thai habit of ถอดรองเท้า (taking your shoes off) indoors. All 22 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations, and word-by-word notes, so the clothing words and classifiers sink in by ear.

Thai often uses kinship terms by relative age as polite address — พี่ ('older sibling') here just means someone a little older, not an actual sibling; ลุง/ป้า (uncle/auntie) and น้อง (younger) work the same way.

A ผ้าถุง is a wrapped tube-skirt worn as comfortable everyday or at-home dress, especially by older women. Note the verb นุ่ง — used for wrapping on lower-body garments like this, where most clothes otherwise take ใส่.

37 ถุงมือ…
ขึ้นดอยลมแรง อย่าลืมเอาถุงมือไปด้วยนะ
It's windy up the mountain — don't forget to bring gloves.
ขึ้น=go upดอย=mountainลมแรง=windyอย่า=don'tลืม=forgetเอา=bringถุงมือ=glovesไปด้วย=alongนะ=(softener)
ดอย is a northern Thai word for a highland mountain (as in Doi Inthanon, Doi Suthep). Unlike the lowlands these uplands genuinely get cold — chilly winter mornings, occasionally near freezing — which is why warm gear like gloves makes sense.
